title: Parading clubs: Buzzards, Commerce Club and others
summary: Describes the clubs George waited for and why the Commerce Club was best.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Do you know that club they call the Buzzards?

I wait for them. I wait for Buzzards. That's all George used to wait for, Buzzards. Then after he left the Buzzards, went to wait for the Lions Club. Of course we used to wait for the El Norah Club. We used to even play the Dancers on Saturday night. But the best club in the city to work for is the Commerce Club. That's the best. The Commerce. The which? Commerce Club from the Garden District. Around Washington? Yeah, starting around Thurid and Chippewa, I think. Called the Connors. That's the best club. You don't do all that walking. They don't. When they leave from Thurid and Chippewa, they go to the part of the region in Annapolis, and they go back and they come on out to Canal Street. Then they come around, and they got buses waiting for you. They take you up to Jefferson Avenue. Then you get off there and you walk, ride the chopper too, to speak. You got a big place there where you go to your hot meal. Then from there you walk on downtown, or they walk like the Mother Club, circling all over the city. Even from Northern Park, Orr-Morke Park, walk to Canal Street, walk back up to Arrheny. I used to do that.

I used to run from one club to the other. I'd follow the lines, the buses from Hardin Park, and then I'd run and catch the Corner Club, and then run and catch the Yellow Jays, and then catch the Garden District.
There were a lot of those clubs.
I don't know how many of them are going there.
They're all of them going. You still got all those clubs. They're all over them. I don't think you'll see much more of the lines club because last time my parade for them,
They didn't have many members. When they got to Canal Street and started back up, if they had 15 members, they had 100, because they had nobody left for the parade.
